record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: For the elliptic equation Delta u = -partial V/partial u, where V is periodic in u and in the spatial variables, suppose that for every slope vector alpha there is a foliation of the torus by graphs of minimal solutions with slope alpha. Must V then be independent of u?

evidence.quote: Does it imply that V is independent of u?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ and consider the elliptic equation
$$\Delta u(x) = -\frac{\partial V}{\partial u}(x,u(x)), \qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^n,$$
where $V:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a smooth function that is periodic of period $1$ in each of the variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$ and periodic of period $1$ in $u$. A classical (smooth) solution $u:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ is called minimal if for every compactly supported smooth perturbation $\varphi$ one has
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\Big(\tfrac12|\nabla(u+\varphi)|^2 - V(x,u+\varphi)\Big)\,dx \ge \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\Big(\tfrac12|\nabla u|^2 - V(x,u)\Big)\,dx.$$
For a vector $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^n$ (the "slope"), a foliation of the torus $\mathbb{T}^{n+1}=\mathbb{R}^{n+1}/\mathbb{Z}^{n+1}$ by minimal solutions of slope $\alpha$ is a $1$-parameter family $\{u_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}}$ of minimal solutions such that $u_\lambda(x)-\alpha\cdot x$ is bounded, $u_\lambda(x)<u_{\lambda'}(x)$ for all $x$ whenever $\lambda<\lambda'$, the graphs $\{(x,u_\lambda(x)):x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}$ project to disjoint hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{T}^{n+1}$ whose union is all of $\mathbb{T}^{n+1}$, and $u_{\lambda+1}=u_\lambda+1$.

Assume that for every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^n$ there exists a foliation of $\mathbb{T}^{n+1}$ by graphs of minimal solutions of slope $\alpha$. Must $V(x,u)$ be independent of $u$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any reference resolving this question on minimal-solution foliations for the periodic elliptic equation $\Delta u=-\partial V/\partial u$. The problem is posed as an open question in the literature on Moser–Bangert minimal foliations, and no proof or counterexample establishing whether the existence of a foliation by minimal solutions of every slope forces $V$ to be independent of $u$ was located.
